memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to Moses, "See, I have made you like God to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron will be your prophet. You are to say everything I command you, and your brother Aaron is to tell Pharaoh to let the Israelites go out of his country."" - Exodus 7:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses had just said, for the second time, that his lips falter. God does not remove the weakness. He arranges around it.

Aaron will be the mouth. Moses will be the one who receives the word. And God says something startling — I have made you like God to Pharaoh. Not that Moses becomes divine, but that he will stand before Pharaoh as God's authorised representative, carrying an authority far above Egypt's throne.

Notice the chain of command. God speaks to Moses, Moses speaks to Aaron, Aaron speaks to Pharaoh. The message must travel unchanged. You are to say everything I command you — not a softened version, not an edited version.

That is the calling of anyone who speaks for God, whether from a pulpit or across a kitchen table. We are not asked to improve God's message or make it more palatable. We are asked to deliver it faithfully.

Paul refused to distort God's word, choosing instead to set forth the truth plainly (2 Cor 4:2). The authority is never in the messenger. It is in the message.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I tempted to soften God's truth to make it easier to deliver?
2. Where has God worked around a weakness rather than removing it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to carry Your word faithfully and not to edit it for comfort. Use me despite my weaknesses. Amen.
